llm.summary: This is a straightforward PDF helper skill with disclosed read, write, and command use for local PDF tasks, with ordinary caution needed around file edits.

dimensions.detail: Local filesystem access and optional command execution are proportionate for parsing and creating PDFs when used on files the user selects.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No executable artifact or install script is present; the skill only documents Python dependency setup, though the dependency notes are somewhat generic and inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The examples use broad natural-language triggers and the mutation guidance is thin, but the actions described remain user-directed PDF operations rather than hidden or unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact shows no persistence, background workers, credential handling, session/profile access, or automatic network exfiltration; writes are limited to PDF outputs or requested page edits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The declared capabilities are PDF reading, creation, text extraction, metadata handling, and basic page operations; read/write/exec permissions are coherent with those local PDF workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want an agent to read and modify local PDF files. Use copies for page deletion or rotation tasks, specify input and output paths clearly, and review any proposed command or file write before allowing it.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Broad PDF-related trigger examples are expected for a PDF utility; they are worth guidance but do not show hidden invocation or purpose-mismatched access.
[SQP-2] expected: PDF creation, rotation, and deletion are disclosed core functions; the lack of explicit backup/overwrite warnings is a usability and data-loss caution, not evidence of malicious or review-level behavior by itself.
